content_voiceover: Now we turn to MEF2D rearranged ALL, a distinct B cell precursor subtype. It shows a striking female predominance of sixty six percent and tends to occur in older children, with a median age of ten point seven years, and nearly sixty percent of patients being ten years or older. On immunophenotype, these blasts frequently express cytoplasmic mu chain in about eighty two percent of cases, CD5 in fifty six percent, and are often CD10 negative, seen in about thirty five percent, which can be a diagnostic clue since most B ALL is CD10 positive. The fusion partner matters prognostically. MEF2D BCL9 is the most common partner, found in fifty four percent of cases, but it carries a worse event free survival of only about sixty five percent. In contrast, MEF2D HNRNPUL1, seen in thirty two percent, has a much better outcome, with event free survival around ninety four percent. Other rarer partners make up the remaining fourteen percent. Overall, with modern therapy, MRD negative remission is achieved in ninety three percent of patients, and five year event free survival is seventy four percent.
keypoints: Female predominance, sixty six percent, and older median age of ten point seven years
Frequent cytoplasmic mu, CD5 positive, and CD10 negative immunophenotype
MEF2D BCL9 partner has worse outcome than MEF2D HNRNPUL1
Overall five year event free survival about seventy four percent
keypoint_voiceover: Key points. MEF2D rearranged ALL favors older girls, with a CD10 negative, CD5 positive immunophenotype. The fusion partner drives prognosis, MEF2D BCL9 does worse, while MEF2D HNRNPUL1 does much better. Overall five year event free survival is around seventy four percent.
